items.followUp: Explain how cohesion between water molecules helps water move upward through xylem.

rubric.why: Credits identifying water loss from leaves as the event that initiates the pull.
rubric.description: States that transpiration or evaporation from leaves creates tension or suction in the xylem.
rubric.how: Look for transpiration or evaporation linked to leaves and the resulting tension or suction.

rubric.why: Credits a force that helps maintain the water column and transmit the pull.
rubric.description: Explains that cohesion between water molecules, or adhesion of water to xylem walls, helps keep the water column continuous so the pull is transmitted upward.
rubric.how: Look for cohesion between water molecules or adhesion to xylem walls, linked to continuity or upward transmission of the pull.

modelAnswer: Transpiration causes evaporation of water from leaf surfaces, creating tension (suction) in the xylem.
Cohesion between water molecules, aided by adhesion to xylem walls, keeps the water column continuous and transmits the pull upward.
